$comment: ★★ CODE AFTER A TERMINATOR, WITH NO LABEL BETWEEN THEM, ASSEMBLES WHERE THE TEXT PUTS IT (P68 round 8, D-ASM-INSTRUCTION-AFTER-A-TERMINATOR-REFUSED and D-ASM-CONDITIONAL-BRANCH-FALLTHROUGH-LAID-OUT-AT-THE-FUNCTION-END). A line after `jmp`, a line after a mid-function `ret`, and a `nop` + `addl` tail after the LAST `ret`, each dead and each changing the exit code if it ran; `jne 2f` falls into the next line. ✔MEASURED 2026-09-23: GNU as 2.42 and clang 18.1.3 run this file to 42. DSS refused the first dead line as code 'it cannot place in a basic block', and laid a conditional branch's fall-through code out after the function's last label. The `.s` walker now plans every block start in pass 1 (label, the line after a conditional branch, the line after any other terminator) and creates the blocks in TEXT order; the dead tail ending `main` closes with the target's unreachable trap. ★ RED-ON-DISABLE: create the anonymous blocks after the labels again (the mint-on-demand order) and the block-plan pin reds — every false edge lands away from its branch. The `release` arm pins only that naming the release pipeline does not break the assembly path (an assembly source forms no HIR/MIR).
